thesis: The plan matches Hugging Face's documented way to publish a dataset — a repository with a CSV and a README.md Dataset card — so it is a workable shape. But no page read shows the dataset page or its rows, so the publish itself and the accuracy of the expected verdicts remain unconfirmed.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The Hugging Face documentation states that a repository hosts all your dataset files, including the revision history, and that users can create a new public or private dataset repository.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The Hugging Face documentation states that clicking Create Dataset Card creates a README.md file in the repository.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The Hugging Face documentation states that text file extensions such as .csv are not tracked by Git LFS by default and that if they are greater than 10MB they will not be committed and uploaded.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The Hub documentation states that the Hub's web interface allows users without developer experience to upload a dataset and that a public dataset is visible to anyone.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The Hub documentation states that the Dataset card metadata fields include license, language and task categories and that these tags help users discover the dataset.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A bee-scouts issue states that the author's Hugging Face account is hivepunk-547-db38b7a4 and that anything it publishes lands only there.

claims.label: FACT

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: The planned dataset's two files fit the documented dataset repository shape: a CSV plus a README.md card.
claims.math: c1 says a repository hosts all the dataset files; c2 says the Dataset card is a README.md in the repository; the plan's CSV plus README.md is therefore the documented two-file form.

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: A small CSV is unlikely to hit the documented 10MB text-file limit.
claims.math: c3 gives the 10MB cutoff for text files; the plan calls the CSV small, so it would sit under that cutoff — but no page gives its actual size.

risks: No page read shows the dataset page itself, so its existence, file list and CSV contents are unconfirmed [https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/datasets-adding]

The account name in the plan differs from the one prior proposals name (hivepunk-547-db38b7a4), so the exact repository path under which it lands is unconfirmed [https://github.com/HivemindOS-Agents/bee-scouts/issues/98]
The expected verdicts in the CSV are only as good as the tool's rules; no page read shows a real run's output backing them [https://huggingface.co/docs/datasets/en/upload_dataset]
Text files such as .csv are not tracked by Git LFS by default, and the docs say text files over 10MB will not be committed [https://huggingface.co/docs/datasets/en/upload_dataset]
